Markus —

Thanks for the catch-up today. As discussed, FinTech Co. is ready to move forward on a 12-month renewal but we need to expand Dedicated capacity across EU and APAC. Attached is our current traffic profile and a proposed capacity uplift (see fintech_capacity_request_v3.xlsx). High-level asks:

- Add a committed EU pool: +32 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved)
- Add a committed APAC pool: +16 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved)
- Global sustained throughput target ~400k tokens/sec with region-aware routing
- 99th pct latency target for 512-token responses: <= 180ms (EU primary; APAC primary for APAC users)
- Failover: cross-region fallback when regional pool is saturated, target failover observed <6s for in-flight requests

We also have commercial questions: impact on discounting, any change to termination rights for added capacity, and whether we can get a commitment level for throughput for pricing purposes. Procurement looped in on cc for contract language.

Can you share a draft amendment and a short ops note on failover behavior? We plan to review internally next week.

Cheers,
Ana Ribeiro
Head of Data Products, FinTech Co.

- Failover: we will configure smart-routing with regional primary and cross-region fallback; the behavior you described is achievable but requires a warm standby and KV-cache replication considerations — ops notes to follow.

I'll put together a draft uplift annex for the renewal and include two commercial options: (A) conservative commit with lower unit discount; (B) higher commit + term extension (18 months) for a deeper discount. Lauren — can you run pricing and provide a redlineable draft? Hannah — can you capture the failover runbook and estimated warm-standby cost? KarThik — please flag any legal/termination constraints we should preempt for Procurement.

Thanks,

Folks — pricing input and proposed commercial options (summary):

Option A — 12mo renewal + uplift (baseline):
- EU reserved: +32 GPUs (list price equivalent)
- APAC reserved: +16 GPUs
- Throughput band (monthly sustained): 350k–420k tokens/sec; breach overage billed per token at $0.0009/token
- Discount: incremental capacity at 22% off list for 12mo
- SLA: 99.5% availability for reserved pools; latency SLO (99th) target <= 180ms measured on 5m rolling windows; credits for SLO breaches capped at one monthly credit up to 10% of monthly dedicated fee

Option B — 18mo commitment (deeper discount + throughput guarantee):
- Same capacity uplift as A
- Discount: incremental capacity at 30% off list
- Guaranteed throughput: committed monthly sustained throughput 400k tokens/sec; overage rate reduced to $0.0006/token
- SLA: Same availability/latency SLO; additional operational review cadence and a quarterly capacity test (joint sim)

Notes on termination: we need legal input on termination for convenience vs. capacity wind-down. KarThik — please advise on a clause that allows us to wind down added capacity with 60d notice if usage materially deviates.

Attached: draft_uplift_annex_2026-12-08.pdf (has redlineable commercial bullets).

Ops notes (summary) — technical considerations for Annex and failover:

1) Topology:
- EU primary pool mapped to eu-central-1 colocations; APAC primary mapped to ap-northeast-1. Pools isolated per-tenant with dedicated node groups.
2) Warm standby & KV cache replication:
- To hit <6s failover target for in-flight requests we need: local KV cache replication every 30s to warm standby in another region OR prefix caching for hot keys. Warm standby cost ~10–12% of reserved pool.
3) Routing & traffic shaping:
- Smart router will prefer regional pool; failover threshold configurable (suggest default 85% queue utilization). When failover occurs, requests will route to nearest compatible model variant.
4) Measurement & SLOs:
- We measure 99th latency on 5m rolling windows per pool. For cross-region failover, latency is measured end-to-end; credits triggered if rolling window shows >2x breach frequency over the month.
5) Maintenance windows and canary:
- Propose a 2-hour weekly maintenance window for region-level kernel upgrades; cross-region canary (5% traffic) during major rollouts.

I'll include these bullets in the draft Annex ops section. Also note network peering and inter-region bandwidth costs not included in reserved fee — call out as separate line item.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
